title: The pullback of module objects preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. The pullback $f^*\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ of module objects
([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]), applied termwise, sends quasi-isomorphisms
between K-flat complexes of $\Lambda_Y$-modules to quasi-isomorphisms
([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal D=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $R=\Lambda_Y$, $R_f=f^*_{\Ab}R$ and $S=\Lambda_X$. Use the small skeletons of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The abelian-group tensor structure of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], together with [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] applied with $\mathcal A=\Ab$, makes $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ abelian monoidal categories with additive tensor product; tensoring preserves colimits, hence is right exact. This verifies the hypotheses on $R\otimes-$, $R_f\otimes-$ and $S\otimes-$ in the lifted-exactness lemma. The functor $F=f^*_{\Ab}$ is strong monoidal by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact], specialized to $\Ab$. Its additivity can also be read directly from finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation: these preserve the zero object, the biproduct injections and projections, hence the diagonal and codiagonal in the formula $u+v=\nabla\circ(u\oplus v)\circ\Delta$. Applying $F$ to this formula gives $F(u+v)=F(u)+F(v)$. By [sk-def-sfb-transport], $G=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ has underlying functor $F$, on both objects and morphisms: $U_{R_f}G=FU_R$. Apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] to these two sheaf categories, $R$, $R_f$, $F$ and $G$. It gives that $G$ is additive and exact.

source.place: Second paragraph, exactness of mapMod(f^*_Ab); expanded using the existing lifted-exactness lemma.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $\alpha_f:R_f\to S$ is an isomorphism for this arbitrary condensed ring and arbitrary scheme morphism. The ring $S=\Lambda_X$ is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], since $\Lambda$ is commutative. The monoid isomorphism $\alpha_f$ also makes $R_f$ commutative. Writing $\tau$ for the symmetry and $a=\alpha_f$, the monoid-map axiom, commutativity of $S$, and naturality of $\tau$ give $$a\circ\mu_{R_f}=\mu_S\circ(a\otimes a)=\mu_S\circ\tau_{S,S}\circ(a\otimes a)=\mu_S\circ(a\otimes a)\circ\tau_{R_f,R_f}=a\circ\mu_{R_f}\circ\tau_{R_f,R_f}.$$ Cancel $a$ to obtain $\mu_{R_f}=\mu_{R_f}\circ\tau_{R_f,R_f}$. In the closed symmetric monoidal abelian sheaf category from step 1, equalizers and coequalizers exist by abelianness, and tensor preserves colimits, so parts 4 and 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] apply: restriction along $\alpha_f^{-1}$ is exact, and $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}$. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}$ is exact. The pullback in the statement is exactly $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ G$ by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Both factors preserve finite limits and finite colimits, so their composite does as well: apply the first factor to a finite limiting or colimiting cone and then the second. A natural isomorphism of functors identifies their image cones, so the displayed isomorphism with restriction also preserves these properties. Restriction is additive since it is the identity on underlying morphisms and their addition. The natural isomorphism transfers this property to extension: conjugating the equality on sums by its components proves additivity. Composing with additive $G$ therefore makes $f^*$ additive and exact.

source.place: Second paragraph, extension along the invertible coefficient morphism and exactness of the composite.

proof.text:
Let $s:P\to P^{\prime}$ be a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of $R$-modules, without any boundedness assumption. The source and target module categories are abelian by the lifted-exactness hypotheses verified in step 1 (also for $S$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact functor $f^*$ from step 2. It gives natural isomorphisms $c^n_K:H^n(f^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*H^n(K)$. Naturality gives the explicit equality
$$H^n(f^*s)=(c^n_{P^{\prime}})^{-1}\circ f^*(H^n(s))\circ c^n_P.$$
Every $H^n(s)$ is invertible by the definition of quasi-isomorphism in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; applying $f^*$ preserves its inverse. The displayed composite is therefore invertible for every $n$, so the same definition says $f^*s$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This applies in particular when $P$ and $P^{\prime}$ are K-flat, proving the assertion.
